messages.subject: Reproducing "Circular Inference" model in Stan - Divergent iterations issue
parts:
I am currently trying to reproduce the circular inference model sketched in this paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms14218 .

When I try to fit the model I get lots of divergent iterations (and Rhat goes wild) and I could use some help in figuring out whether I'm making a trivial mistake somewhere, or as Michael Betancourt mentioned on Twitter "Your model is multimodal or has an awkward geometry and needs reparameterization". In that case, i could use some help in figuring out the best way of tacking that.

Sample Data (5 out of ca 80 participants): https://www.dropbox.com/s/g6jcj85a3w6gscg/d2.csv?dl=0

The task is a gumball task, where participants have to guess whether the next gumball extracted is red (or green). The dataset includes: 
  • Participant Number, 
  • ChoiceRed: whether the participant indicated the next gumball is red or not
  • Self: an index of how many red gumballs the participant has seen in the urn (expressed on a scale from 0 to 1)
  • lSelf: the logit of Self
  • Others: an index of how many other people the participant sees guessing red (expressed on a scale from 0 to 1)
  • lOthers: the logit of Others

First as a sanity check I implemented a weighted bayesian model (using the rethinking package as a crutch), which gives a few divergences, but nice traceplots and Rhats=1 on both simulated and real data. The model follows the paper previously linked, only adding the possibility for biases towards red (no matter the info) with a[Participant] and pooling information across participants.



data{
    int<lower=1> N;
    int<lower=1> N_Participant;
    int ChoiceRed[N];
    int Participant[N];
    real lSelf[N];
    real lOthers[N];
}
parameters{
    vector[N_Participant] a;
    real muA;
    vector[N_Participant] wOthers;
    real muO;
    vector[N_Participant] wSelf;
    real muS;
}
model{
    vector[N] mu;
    muS ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
    wSelf ~ normal( muS , 0.3 );
    muO ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
    wOthers ~ normal( muO , 0.3 );
    muA ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
    a ~ normal( muA , 0.1 );
    for ( i in 1:N ) {
        mu[i] = a[Participant[i]] + log((wSelf[Participant[i]] * exp(lSelf[i]) + 1 - wSelf[Participant[i]])/((1 -      wSelf[Participant[i]]) * exp(lSelf[i]) + wSelf[Participant[i]])) +      log((wOthers[Participant[i]] * exp(lOthers[i]) + 1 - wOthers[Participant[i]])/((1 -          wOthers[Participant[i]]) * exp(lOthers[i]) + wOthers[Participant[i]]));
    }
    ChoiceRed ~ binomial_logit( 1 , mu );
}
generated quantities{
    vector[N] mu;
    real dev;
    dev = 0;
    for ( i in 1:N ) {
        mu[i] = a[Participant[i]] + log((wSelf[Participant[i]] * exp(lSelf[i]) + 1 - wSelf[Participant[i]])/((1 -      wSelf[Participant[i]]) * exp(lSelf[i]) + wSelf[Participant[i]])) +      log((wOthers[Participant[i]] * exp(lOthers[i]) + 1 - wOthers[Participant[i]])/((1 -          wOthers[Participant[i]]) * exp(lOthers[i]) + wOthers[Participant[i]]));
    }
    dev = dev + (-2)*binomial_logit_lpmf( ChoiceRed | 1 , mu );
}

messages.subject: Re: Reproducing "Circular Inference" model in Stan - Divergent iterations issue
parts:
I don't know about the model you're showing, but I think your idea of using functions to clean up your code is good. Maybe it's just a bug that's making the inference hard. I removed the generated quantities section for brevity (but you should go ahead and add it back). I only tested that this compiles. I did *not* actually do a sampling, so double check me, but rewriting your harder problem with Fs might make it easier to see what's going on.

functions {
  real F(real L, real w) {
    real eL = exp(L);

    return log((w * eL + 1 - w)/((1 - w) * eL + w));

}
}

data{
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> N_Participant;
  int ChoiceRed[N];
  int Participant[N];
  real lSelf[N];
  real lOthers[N];
}

parameters{
  vector[N_Participant] a;
  real muA;
  vector[N_Participant] wOthers;
  real muO;
  vector[N_Participant] wSelf;
  real muS;
}

model{
  vector[N] mu;
  muS ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
  wSelf ~ normal( muS , 0.3 );
  muO ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
  wOthers ~ normal( muO , 0.3 );
  muA ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
  a ~ normal( muA , 0.1 );

  for ( i in 1:N ) {
mu[i] = a[Participant[i]] + F(lSelf[i], wSelf[Participant[i]]) + F(lOthers[i], wOthers[Participant[i]]);

}

  ChoiceRed ~ binomial_logit( 1 , mu );
}
Ben

and wOthers.

ChoiceRed ~ bernoulli_logit(mu);

On Sunday, April 23, 2017 at 5:03:14 PM UTC+2, Riccardo Fusaroli wrote:

I am currently trying to reproduce the circular inference model sketched in this paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms14218 .

When I try to fit the model I get lots of divergent iterations (and Rhat goes wild) and I could use some help in figuring out whether I'm making a trivial mistake somewhere, or as Michael Betancourt mentioned on Twitter "Your model is multimodal or has an awkward geometry and needs reparameterization". In that case, i could use some help in figuring out the best way of tacking that.

Sample Data (5 out of ca 80 participants): https://www.dropbox.com/s/g6jcj85a3w6gscg/d2.csv?dl=0

The task is a gumball task, where participants have to guess whether the next gumball extracted is red (or green). The dataset includes: 
  • Participant Number, 
  • ChoiceRed: whether the participant indicated the next gumball is red or not
  • Self: an index of how many red gumballs the participant has seen in the urn (expressed on a scale from 0 to 1)
  • lSelf: the logit of Self
  • Others: an index of how many other people the participant sees guessing red (expressed on a scale from 0 to 1)
  • lOthers: the logit of Others

First as a sanity check I implemented a weighted bayesian model (using the rethinking package as a crutch), which gives a few divergences, but nice traceplots and Rhats=1 on both simulated and real data. The model follows the paper previously linked, only adding the possibility for biases towards red (no matter the info) with a[Participant] and pooling information across participants.



data{
    int<lower=1> N;
    int<lower=1> N_Participant;
    int ChoiceRed[N];
    int Participant[N];
    real lSelf[N];
    real lOthers[N];
}
parameters{
    vector[N_Participant] a;
    real muA;
    vector[N_Participant] wOthers;
    real muO;
    vector[N_Participant] wSelf;
    real muS;
}
model{
    vector[N] mu;
    muS ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
    wSelf ~ normal( muS , 0.3 );
    muO ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
    wOthers ~ normal( muO , 0.3 );
    muA ~ normal( 0.5 , 0.1 );
    a ~ normal( muA , 0.1 );

messages.subject: Re: Reproducing "Circular Inference" model in Stan - Divergent iterations issue
parts:
I don't know about the divergent iterations thing, but if you have a low neff and a high Rhat, it'd be a good idea to go look at the posterior distributions/traceplots.

You might look at the posterior distributions of each chain to make sure everything is converging to the same solution. Multimodal distributions could give these the Rhat/neff metrics trouble I think.

You might also look at pairplots for your parameters too see if things are really tightly correlated. Maybe there are identifiability issues that are giving the sampler problems (that could be addressed with some priors).

Do you have simulated data for this problem? Might also scale around the size of the data and see if anything changes if so.
